topic: Did Christ have a biological father?
cr1:
DEFENDER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

**POSITION.** The answer is yes: the child had a biological father, and the text names him — Joseph, "of the house and lineage of David." This is argued from the promised seed's own words, from the naming rows, from the meaning of the words "of the Holy Ghost" and "Son of God," and from the timing rows held as written.

---

**I. THE SEED THE PROMISE REQUIRES IS SEED OUT OF A MAN'S BODY — [L1], [L2]**

[L1] 2 Samuel 7:12 — "And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, **which shall proceed out of thy bowels**, and I will establish his kingdom." The promise to David is a seed that proceeds out of his own body.
[L1] Psalm 132:11 — "The LORD hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; **Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne**."
[L1] Acts 2:30 — "Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that **of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh**, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
[L1] Romans 1:3 — "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, **which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh**."

[L2] The words themselves: *mimme'eykha* (out of thy bowels) at 2 Samuel 7:12; *sperma* (seed) and *kata sarka* (according to the flesh) at Romans 1:3; *osphys* (loins) at Acts 2:30 — the same loins-word the writer of Hebrews uses of Levi being in the body of Abraham.
[L3] Hebrews 7:9-10 — "And as I may so say, Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham. **For he was yet in the loins of his father**, when Melchisedec met him." That is how the canon pictures descent through a father's body. Hebrews 7:14 adds of this child: "it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."

So whatever else is said about this conception, the promised child must be seed out of a man's body. A legal claim, an adoption, or a title produces no such seed (the rows above say body, bowels, loins, flesh).

---

**II. THE CANON'S STATED MEANS OF BEGETTING IS THE HUSBAND KNOWING HIS WIFE — [L1], [L2], [L3]**

[L1] Genesis 4:1 — "And Adam **knew** Eve his wife: and she conceived, and bare Cain." That is the canon's own sentence for how a child is begotten.
[L2] The verb is the knowing-word (*ginōskō*, know) — the same family the conception rows use in the negative: Matthew 1:25 "knew her not" (*ouk eginōsken*, he was not knowing her) and Luke 1:34 "I know not a man" (*andra ou ginōskō*, I know not a man, present tense).
[L3] The row in which those negatives stand is a marriage row — Matthew 1:18-25 — and it speaks of husband and wife throughout: "Joseph her husband" (1:19), "Mary thy wife" (1:20), and the child is named by the man (1:21, 1:25).

---

**III. THE FATHER IS NAMED — JOSEPH — IN FIVE REGISTERS OF THE TEXT — [L1], [L3]**

[L1] The mother's own mouth: Luke 2:48 — "behold, **thy father and I** have sought thee sorrowing."
[L1] The narrator: Luke 2:33 — "**Joseph and his mother** marvelled"; Luke 2:41 — "**his parents** went to Jerusalem."
[L1] The town: Luke 4:22 — "Is not this **Joseph's son**?"; John 6:42 — "Is not this Jesus, **the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know**?"
[L1] A disciple: John 1:45 — "Jesus of Nazareth, **the son of Joseph**."
[L1] The angel: Matthew 1:20 — "**Joseph, thou son of David**"; Luke 1:27 — Mary was "espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, **of the house of David**"; Luke 2:4 — "because he was **of the house and lineage of David**"; Luke 1:32 — "the Lord God shall give unto him **the throne of his father David**."

[L3] Joseph names the child: Matthew 1:21 "**thou** shalt call his name JESUS" and 1:25 "he called his name JESUS" — the father's act, exactly as Zacharias names John (Luke 1:13, 1:62-63). And the reckoning of Israel is by the father's house: Numbers 1:2 — "by their families, **by the house of their fathers**, with the number of their names, every male by their polls." No line of descent through a mother is named anywhere in the canon's registers.

---

**IV. "OF THE HOLY GHOST" AND "SON OF GOD" DO NOT SAY WHO BEGAT THE CHILD — [L1], [L2], [L3]**

[L1] Matthew 1:20, quoted whole as it stands in its row: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived [margin: Gr. begotten] in her is **of the Holy Ghost**."

[L2] "of" is *ek* (of, out of). Where the New Testament says one is *ek* of God or of the Spirit, it names origin in the covenant sense, never biological fatherhood: John 1:13 "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, **but of God**"; 1 John 3:9 "born of God"; 1 John 5:1. Where the text means flesh descent it adds the marker — Romans 1:3 "of the seed of David **according to the flesh**" (*kata sarka*). Matthew 1:20 has no such marker.
[L2] The angel's own verbs are presence and power, not begetting. *Eperchomai* (come upon) is used of the apostles — Acts 1:8 "ye shall receive power, after that **the Holy Ghost is come upon you**"; and *episkiazō* (overshadow) is used of the transfiguration cloud (Luke 9:34 "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them") and of Peter's healing shadow (Acts 5:15 "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them"). Neither word denotes begetting at any row.

[L1] And the title "Son of God" is a covenant title given beside a human father: 1 Chronicles 28:6 — "**Solomon thy son**, he shall build my house and my courts: for **I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father**." Solomon had a father; the title does not describe who begat him. So with this child: Psalm 2:7 "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee" is applied to the resurrection — Acts 13:33 "in that he hath **raised up Jesus again**"; Romans 1:4 "declared to be the Son of God ... **by the resurrection from the dead**."

---

**V. THE TIMING ROWS, HELD AS WRITTEN, BOUND THE ABSTINENCE TO THE PREGNANCY — [L1], [L2], [L3]**

[L1] Matthew 1:18 — "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, **before they came together**, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." That dates the finding, not the father.
[L1] Matthew 1:19 — "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." [L2] The words state intent and two grounds — just (*dikaios*, righteous), and unwilling to make a public example; there is no verb of knowing or of finding-fault in the row.
[L1] Matthew 1:24-25 — "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and **took unto him his wife**: And **knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son**: and he called his name JESUS." [L2] "till" (*heōs hou*, until) bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy and stops at the birth; the row ends with the husband naming the child.
[L1] Luke 1:34 — "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing **I know not a man**?" [L2] *andra ou ginōskō* (I know not a man) is present tense — her state at the moment of the question; a vow of permanent abstinence would not be written that way.
[L3] From the espousal they are husband and wife in law: Matthew 1:19 "Joseph her husband"; 1:20 "Mary thy wife"; and the law calls a betrothed woman a wife — Deuteronomy 22:24 "hath humbled **his neighbour's wife**."

One anticipatory word: the Hebrew of Isaiah 7:14 is *ha-almah* (the young woman) — the word for a virgin, *bethulah* (virgin), is a different word and is not used there — and the sign is bounded within Isaiah's own day (Isaiah 7:16 "before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good"; 8:3-4, 8). A translation's word "virgin" does not answer who the child's father is; the naming rows answer that.

---

**VI. CONCLUSION AND THE RULED SENTENCE**

[L4] — footing shown: from [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12, Psalm 132:11, Acts 2:30, Romans 1:3 (the seed must be of a man's body) and [L2] the body-words themselves (*mimme'eykha*, out of thy bowels; *osphys*, loins; *kata sarka*, according to the flesh), joined by [L1] Genesis 4:1 and [L2] the knowing-word (*ginōskō*, know) — the canon's stated means of begetting — together with [L1] the five naming registers (Luke 2:48; 2:33; John 6:42; John 1:45; Matthew 1:20) and [L3] Joseph's naming act at Matthew 1:21, 25 with Luke 1:13: Joseph, of the house of David, knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins. A man was involved; the man is named.

Two rows are held as written and are not set aside: Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child," and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" — the second bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy, the first dates the finding. Neither row says there was no father; and the seed rows forbid the sentence "no man was involved," because the promised seed must proceed out of a man's body and be of the flesh of David.

---

**DECLARED CHAIN**

D1. The promised seed must proceed out of a man's body — [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12 "which shall proceed out of thy bowels," Psalm 132:11 "of the fruit of thy body," Acts 2:30 "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh," Romans 1:3 "made of the seed of David according to the flesh"; [L2] *mimme'eykha* (out of thy bowels), *osphys* (loins), *kata sarka* (according to the flesh); [L3] Hebrews 7:9-10 (Levi in the loins of his father).

D2. The canon's stated means of begetting is the husband knowing his wife — [L1] Genesis 4:1 "Adam knew Eve his wife: and she conceived," Matthew 1:25 "knew her not"; [L2] *ginōskō* (know), the same verb family in both rows; [L3] the marriage row Matthew 1:18-25 ("Joseph her husband," "Mary thy wife").

D3. The father is named — Joseph, of the house and lineage of David — [L1] Luke 2:48 "thy father and I," Luke 2:33 "Joseph and his mother," John 6:42 "the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know," John 1:45 "the son of Joseph," Matthew 1:20 "Joseph, thou son of David," Luke 2:4 "of the house and lineage of David"; [L3] Joseph names the child at Matthew 1:21, 25 with Luke 1:13, 62-63, and reckoning is "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2).

D4. "Of the Holy Ghost" marks covenant origin, and "Son of God" is a covenant title — neither names a begetter — [L2] *ek* (of) with God/Spirit at John 1:13 "born of God," 1 John 3:9, 5:1, with no *kata sarka* (according to the flesh) at Matthew 1:20, and the angel's verbs *eperchomai* (come upon) at Acts 1:8 and *episkiazō* (overshadow) at Luke 9:34 and Acts 5:15; [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6 "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him to be my son," with Psalm 2:7 applied at Acts 13:33 (the resurrection) and Romans 1:4.

D5. The timing rows, held as written, bound the abstinence to the pregnancy and state a present state — [L1] Matthew 1:18, 1:25, Luke 1:34; [L2] *ouk eginōsken ... heōs hou* (knew her not till) and *andra ou ginōskō* (I know not a man, present tense); [L3] espousal makes husband and wife in law (Deuteronomy 22:24 "his neighbour's wife").

D6. ANSWER: Yes — Christ had a biological father: Joseph, of the house and lineage of David, knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins; the promised seed of David came by the flesh as the promise requires — [L4] footed on [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12, Acts 2:30, Romans 1:3, Genesis 4:1, Matthew 1:25, Luke 2:48, John 6:42 and [L2] *ginōskō* (know), *kata sarka* (according to the flesh), *osphys* (loins), with [L3] Hebrews 7:9-10 and Matthew 1:21-25.

# CHALLENGE: The text says no man begat the child

The defender's answer is that Joseph begat him. I hold the standard reading: no human father begat Jesus, and the child was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost. I take his five points in order and then put the positive case.

---

## I. The defender's own timing rows exclude Joseph at the conception (answer to D5)

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, **before they came together**, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] *synerchomai* (to come together) is the word for the marriage union. [L3] 1 Corinthians 7:5 uses it of husband and wife: "come together again." The conception was therefore already present before the union began.
[L1] Matthew 1:25: Joseph "**knew her not** till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:18 puts the child in the womb before the union, and Matthew 1:25, which the defender himself reads as binding abstinence through the pregnancy, gives no knowing through the birth. The conception falls inside both windows, so Joseph did not know Mary at the conception. The defender's D5 concedes the second window. The first window ("before they came together") is stated in the text, and no verse says Joseph knew Mary within the espousal. His sentence "Joseph… knew Mary his wife within the espousal" has no verse behind it.

## II. Joseph's reaction and the angel's answer make no sense if Joseph was the father (answer to D5)

[L1] Matthew 1:19: Joseph, "being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L2] *deigmatizō* (to make a public example, to expose to shame) and *apolyō* (to release, put away).
[L3] Deuteronomy 22:23-24 prescribes stoning for a betrothed woman who lies with another. The defender himself brings in that verse to call her a wife. That law is why a public example was possible.
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: **for** that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] *gar* (for, because) gives the reason Joseph need not fear.

[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:19 shows a just man treating the pregnancy as a ground for putting her away. Deuteronomy 22:23-24 shows what the pregnancy would mean if another man were the cause. Matthew 1:20 shows the angel removing the fear by naming the Holy Ghost as the source ("for…"). If Joseph were the father, he had no ground to put her away and the angel's "for" answers nothing. The defender says there is "no verb of… finding-fault" in the row. The words "put her away" and "publick example" supply it.

## III. "Of the Holy Ghost" names the source of the begetting (answer to D4)

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived [margin: begotten] in her is of the Holy Ghost." The defender quotes the margin himself.
[L2] *gennaō* (to beget, to bear) is the verb of the whole genealogy: "Abraham begat Isaac" (Matthew 1:2). Here it takes *ek* (out of) with *pneumatos hagiou* (Holy Ghost). [L3] In the same chapter *ek* with a parent names the source of the birth: Matthew 1:3 "Phares and Zara **of** Thamar" (*ek tēs Thamar*, out of Thamar). The same preposition in the same book and chapter names the source of bodily birth.
[L2] The defender cites John 1:13, but the verse reads "not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, **nor of the will of man**, but of God." It sets *ek* God against *ek* man as exclusive sources, and its context is regeneration.
[L1] Luke 1:35 gives the reason for the title: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: **therefore also** that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] *dio kai* (therefore also) makes the conception the ground of the title.

[L4] Footing: Luke 1:35's "therefore" and Matthew 1:3's *ek* show that the title rests on how he was conceived and that *ek* names the begetting source. The defender's Solomon parallel (1 Chronicles 28:6, "I have chosen him") gives choice as the ground. Luke gives conception as the ground. His Acts 13:33 point also fails: *anistēmi* (to raise up) there means bringing onto the scene, as with "raised up unto them David" (Acts 13:22). The resurrection is introduced separately in 13:34 with "**as concerning that** he raised him up **from the dead**."

## IV. The defender's reading leaves Luke 1:34-37 without an answer (answer to D2 and D5)

[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:27 has just called her "a virgin" twice (*parthenos*, virgin) while "espoused to a man whose name was Joseph."
[L2] *epei* (since, seeing that) makes her present state the ground of the difficulty. If the answer were "by the man you are betrothed to," there would be no "how."
[L1] The angel does not answer "by Joseph." He answers "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee" (1:35), and then adds, "For with God **nothing shall be impossible**" (1:37). [L2] *adynateō* (to be impossible) is the same word the angel uses of the old woman Elisabeth's conception in 1:36.

[L4] Footing: Luke 1:34 supplies the question and 1:35 and 1:37 supply the answer. The defender's own concession that *eperchomai* (come upon) and *episkiazō* (overshadow) are not words of begetting means that, on his reading, the angel's reply gives Mary no mechanism. The text instead presents the reply as the whole mechanism: the Holy Ghost, in the place where a man's knowing would stand. Genesis 4:1 gives the ordinary means, and nobody disputes it. Luke 1:34-37 states that this conception was not by that means.

## V. The genealogy, which the defender never touches, breaks the pattern at Joseph (answer to D3)

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the **husband of Mary**, **of whom** was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L2] Every earlier link is *egennēsen* (begat), active, from father to son. The last link changes. Joseph is *anēr* (husband), and the birth is *egennēthē* (was born, passive) *ex hēs* (of whom, feminine singular), so Mary alone is named as the source.
[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (**as was supposed**) the son of Joseph."
[L2] *enomizeto* (was supposed, was reckoned).
[L1] Luke 2:48-49: Mary says, "thy father and I have sought thee." The child answers, "wist ye not that I must be about **my Father's** business?"

[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:16's changed grammar and Luke 3:23's "as was supposed" show that the narrators distinguish the reputed father from the begetter. Luke 2:49 corrects Luke 2:48 on the spot. As for the defender's other naming rows, Luke 4:22 and John 6:42 are the crowd's words, and in John 6:41-42 the same speakers murmur at his saying "I came down from heaven." Luke 2:33's "his parents" and "Joseph and his mother" describe legal standing. Joseph's naming of the child (Matthew 1:21, 25) is likewise an act of legal acceptance. He is told "take unto thee Mary thy wife" (1:20), which is an act of taking, not of begetting.

## VI. The seed rows do not require Joseph's loins (answer to D1)

[L1] Genesis 3:15: "**her seed**." The first promise names the seed of the woman. [L2] *zera'* (seed) is attached to *ishshah* (woman).
[L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, **made of a woman**." [L2] *genomenon ek gynaikos* (become out of a woman) names no man. Romans 1:3 uses *ginomai* (to become), not *gennaō* (to beget), for "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
[L1] Jeremiah 22:30: of Coniah, "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah." [L1] Matthew 1:11-12 places Jechonias in Joseph's line.
[L3] Daughters carried an inheritance and a line: Numbers 27:1-11. Ezra 2:61 says a man "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai… and was called after their name." Luke 3:31 runs a line through Nathan, son of David, while Matthew 1:6 runs through Solomon. [L4] On this footing the Davidic flesh comes through Mary, and Joseph's line through Jechonias is under the Jeremiah 22:30 bar. Matthew 1:16 gives Joseph the legal standing and does not make him the father. The throne belongs by Luke 1:32 to "his father David," spoken to Mary.

## VII. Isaiah 7:14 as Matthew reads it (answer to the "anticipatory word")

[L1] Isaiah 7:11, 14: the LORD offers a sign "in the depth, or in the height above," and gives "a sign": "Behold, a virgin shall conceive." Matthew 1:22-23 says "all this was done" to fulfil it, and writes *parthenos* (virgin).
[L2] *ha-almah* (the maiden). [L3] The KJV renders the same word "virgin" at Genesis 24:43, of Rebekah, whom Genesis 24:16 calls *bethulah* (virgin) and adds "neither had any man known her." The two words name the same person. [L3] Joel 1:8 uses *bethulah* of a woman mourning "the husband of her youth," so the defender's sharp division of the words does not hold in the canon.
[L1] Isaiah 8:3 names a different child, Maher-shalal-hash-baz, and the name Immanuel is not given there.

[L4] Footing: Isaiah 7:11-14 requires a sign that is extraordinary, and an ordinary conception by a married woman is no sign. Genesis 24:16 and 24:43 show *almah* used of a virgin, and Matthew 1:22-23 reads the verse that way. Matthew 1:23 shows the apostle's reading, and the defender has offered no verse that overrides it.

---

## DECLARED CHAIN (challenger)

C1. The child was begotten in Mary before any union with Joseph, so Joseph is excluded at the conception. [L1] Matthew 1:18, 1:25; [L2] *synerchomai* (to come together); [L3] 1 Corinthians 7:5.
C2. Joseph's intent to put Mary away and the angel's "for" presuppose that he was not the father. [L1] Matthew 1:19-20; [L2] *deigmatizō* (to make a public example), *gar* (for); [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23-24.
C3. "Of the Holy Ghost" names the begetting source, and "therefore" grounds the title Son of God in the conception. [L1] Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35; [L2] *gennaō* (to beget), *ek* (out of), *dio kai* (therefore also); [L3] Matthew 1:3, John 1:13.
C4. Luke 1:34-37 states that the conception was without the ordinary means. [L1] Luke 1:27, 1:34-37; [L2] *epei* (since), *adynateō* (to be impossible); [L3] Genesis 4:1 as the ordinary rule the passage sets aside.
C5. The text distinguishes the reputed father from the begetter. [L1] Matthew 1:16, Luke 3:23, Luke 2:48-49; [L2] *egennēthē ex hēs* (was born of whom, feminine), *enomizeto* (was supposed).
C6. The seed rows are satisfied through Mary, and Joseph's line is barred by Jeremiah 22:30. [L1] Genesis 3:15, Galatians 4:4, Jeremiah 22:30, Matthew 1:11-12; [L2] *genomenon ek gynaikos* (become out of a woman); [L3] Numbers 27:1-11, Ezra 2:61.

**ANSWER: No.** The text gives Jesus no human biological father. Joseph was the husband of Mary and the legal father who took her and named the child, and the child was conceived in her by the Holy Ghost.

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Terms.** By "biological father" I mean a human male whose seed contributed to the conception of the child. I affirm that Mary conceived by the Holy Ghost with no man's contribution. **[L1]** "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" (Matt 1:18).
- **[L2]** *synelthein* (to come together) is a verb of marital union. *Prin ē* (before) places the conception ahead of any union. *Ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of Spirit holy) uses *ek* (out of), the preposition of source and origin.

**[L1]** "That which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matt 1:20).
- **[L2]** *to gennēthen* (the thing begotten or conceived) is again followed by *ek pneumatos* (out of the Spirit). The text gives the source of the conception, and the source is not a man.

**[L1]** Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (Matt 1:25).
- **[L2]** *ginōskō* (to know) is the Hebrew idiom of marital knowing, as in Gen 4:1. It is the same verb Mary uses in Luke 1:34.
